milestones.antecedent: Mata v. Avianca — Rule 11 sanctions for fabricated ChatGPT citations
milestones.binding: Couvrette v. Wisnovsky — ~$110K penalty for 15 fake cases, 8 fabricated quotes
milestones.note: First Rule 11 sanction for fabricated citations to the first six-figure penalty. The antecedent is a T1 court order on the record 906 days before the binding escalation; no prediction was needed, only reading.

milestones.antecedent: Ex Parte Allen Michael Lee v. the State of Texas — AI filing certification (Judge Starr standing order)
milestones.binding: California Rule of Court 10.430 — courts must adopt generative-AI policies
milestones.note: A single Texas court's filing certification preceded a statewide rule requiring every California court to adopt a generative-AI policy by 730 days. One judge is a precursor, not a forecast.

milestones.antecedent: EU Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 — software and AI are 'products'
milestones.binding: EU AI Act obligations take effect
milestones.note: Directive passage to obligations taking effect, 601 days. Legislative lead time is the longest and the most observable: passage is a dated, public, tier-1 fact.

milestones.antecedent: Florida Bar Ethics Opinion 24-1 — self-learning AI and client confidentiality
milestones.binding: ABA Formal Opinion 512 — Generative AI Tools
milestones.note: First state bar opinion on generative AI to the national opinion, 192 days. State-then-national is the standard adoption path for a professional-responsibility control.

milestones.antecedent: ABA Formal Opinion 512 — Generative AI Tools
milestones.binding: In Re Amendments to Arkansas RPC — AI competence under Rule 5.3
milestones.note: National guidance to a binding rule amendment, 500 days. Guidance is the precursor that makes the eventual rule unsurprising.

milestones.antecedent: France criminalizes judicial profiling (Justice Reform Act, Art. 33)
milestones.binding: Ross v. United States — judicial AI competency and bias duty
milestones.note: A foreign statute to a US duty holding, 2,161 days. The longest lead on the record and the weakest to act on: foreign law is a signal, not a domestic obligation.

milestones.antecedent: EU Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 — software and AI are 'products'
milestones.binding: Nippon Life v. OpenAI — first AI-vendor-liability lawsuit
milestones.note: Treating AI software as a 'product' to the first AI-vendor-liability suit, 451 days. The liability theory predates the litigation that tests it.

milestones.antecedent: Stanford/Yale 'Large Legal Fictions' — 58–88% hallucination rate on legal queries
milestones.binding: Stanford: Westlaw AI 34% error rate, Lexis+ AI 17%
milestones.note: An academic demonstration of the capability gap to named, per-tool error rates, 872 days. This is the L1 capability curve moving, tracked as its own order.

milestones.antecedent: White v. County of Suffolk — AI availability and fee reasonableness
milestones.binding: Virginia LEO 1901 — value-based billing need not shrink when AI cuts time
milestones.note: A fee-reasonableness ruling to a bar opinion holding that value-based billing need not shrink when AI cuts time, 333 days. The economic control follows the case law.

milestones.antecedent: Colorado AI Act — NIST/ISO 42001 affirmative defense, § 6-1-1706
milestones.binding: Colorado repeals and replaces its AI Act (SB 26-189) — narrower transparency law
milestones.note: NOT a landed pair. Included as the honest counter-case: a state AI act enacted in February was repealed and replaced by May. An antecedent does not guarantee the binding event; direction shifts are exactly what the radar admits it cannot forecast.

milestones.antecedent: CNA adds AI governance to malpractice underwriting
milestones.note: Underwriting signal with no binding event yet. The finding worth watching is the absence: as of this record no insurer requires a certified AI tool as a condition of coverage. A pending milestone is a result, not a gap.

milestones.antecedent: AI LEAD Act (S.2937) — proposed federal AI product liability standards
milestones.note: Two proposed federal bills (AI LEAD Act, AI AGENT Act) and an EU Commission draft on agentic systems, none binding. Highest-pressure pending control on the board; the firms that will be ready are the ones building authorization-and-logging now.
